rubrics.rubric: Does the workbook independently reconcile every preliminary CSV quantity and make each adopted value reproducible?
criterion: The Excel workbook contains exactly the Data Verification, Quantity Takeoff, Engineer's Estimate, and Cost Summary tabs.
The Data Verification sheet contains one row for every computed quantity in Bridge_CR42_Dimensions_and_Quantities.csv.
Each reconciliation row provides the CSV value with units, the independently calculated value with units, percent difference, a greater-than-2-percent flag, and a resolution note.
Each reconciliation row shows the dimensions, geometry, counts, and assumptions needed to reproduce the independent calculation.
Percent difference is calculated as the absolute CSV-to-calculated difference divided by the calculated value, and values within 2 percent are marked verified while larger differences are flagged.
A quantity that cannot be independently resolved from the named inputs is identified as provisional with the missing design input stated instead of being presented as verified.

rubrics.rubric: Are the adopted bridge quantities calculated accurately from the named inputs and carried into the quantity takeoff with the required rounding conventions?
criterion: Existing deck removal uses the stated 9,567.5-square-foot deck area and 7.5-inch existing thickness, yielding approximately 221.5 cubic yards rather than the CSV value of 597.3 cubic yards.
New deck concrete uses the full out-to-out deck area and 8-inch thickness, yielding approximately 236.2 cubic yards and resolving the CSV's inconsistent area description.
Expansion-joint length accounts for the 15-degree skew, yielding approximately 92.1 linear feet for the two abutments.

Epoxy-coated reinforcing quantity is independently checked using the CSV's stated 6-percent-of-slab-weight basis, yielding approximately 57,400 pounds unless a different source-supported design basis is documented.
Haunch concrete is checked only with source-supported dimensions, and any missing girder-flange width or equivalent design input is explicitly identified before the quantity is adopted.
The remaining CSV quantities are independently checked, and the Quantity Takeoff sheet applies the Alaska DOT guide's applicable rounding conventions to the adopted values.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Engineer's Estimate use traceable CDOT bid items, adopted quantities, and the required unit-price hierarchy?
criterion: Each estimate row includes an actual applicable CDOT 2024 item code, description, quantity, unit, unit price, price source, and extended cost.
Estimate quantities agree with the adopted values in the reconciliation and quantity-takeoff sheets.
The CDOT 2024 Cost Data Book is used for every bid item it covers.
A Michigan LAP or Alaska DOT Table 8-2 price is used only when the item is unavailable in the CDOT source, with any regional adjustment or unit conversion documented.
Extended costs are mathematically correct and every price can be traced to the cited source entry.

rubrics.rubric: Does the estimate total only the authorized base scope and calculate the required cost summary correctly?
criterion: The base estimate matches the authorized scope in the project memo.
A repair or add-alternate outside the authorized scope is excluded from the base total or clearly separated as optional.
The Cost Summary calculates the construction subtotal and mobilization at 10 percent.

The Cost Summary calculates contingency at 20 percent and construction engineering at 15 percent, states the displayed bases, and includes mobilization in the construction-engineering base as instructed.
The grand total reconciles to the estimate rows and the displayed markups.

rubrics.rubric: Does the value-engineering CSV present a source-grounded 30-year comparison of full replacement and HPC overlay?
criterion: The value-engineering deliverable is a CSV comparing full deck replacement with HPC overlay.
Both alternatives list their included scope components, quantities or cost bases, unit prices, price sources, initial cost, assumed service life, and 30-year lifecycle cost.
The HPC overlay uses the Michigan LAP Deep Overlay unit price with an explicitly stated Region 1 adjustment factor.
Lifecycle calculations are reproducible and apply the documented service-life and renewal assumptions consistently.
The final row states a 30-year recommendation supported by the calculated costs, service-life assumptions, and relevant project risks.
An equivalent supported lifecycle method or recommendation is accepted when its assumptions and uncertainty are documented.

rubrics.rubric: Does the one-page summary memo communicate the estimate, data findings, and source-grounded design risks required by the instructions?
criterion: The memo is no more than one page and states the reconciled project total.
The memo identifies the principal cost drivers.
The memo summarizes the material data-quality discrepancies and their adopted resolutions.
The memo identifies at least three distinct risks requiring further design input.
The risks include a specific environmental constraint and a specific construction-timing or scheduling risk supported by the named project sources.
